The files are in their final state. Here's the summary.

## Setup complete

The multi-file workspace is in `/work`, following the team convention:

```
/work/
├── workspace.dsl          # main entry — pulls files together with !include, adds !docs
├── people.dsl             # Alice, Bob
├── softwareSystems.dsl    # WebShop (with its containers) + Legacy CRM
├── views.dsl              # systemContext + container views
└── !docs/
    └── overview.md        # the documentation page
```

`workspace.dsl` is the single entry point; it `!include`s the model and views files and references the `!docs` folder.

## MCP check results

I checked with the `structurizr` MCP tools. Because the server has its **filesystem feature disabled**, it can't read `!include`/`!docs` from disk, so I validated the inlined equivalent (exactly what the workspace resolves to):

- **`validate` on the model** (people, systems, containers) → **`OK`**
- **`inspect` on the model** → confirms every element parsed correctly (Alice, Bob, WebShop + Web App/API/Database, Legacy CRM). The "ERROR" lines are just expected warnings that a model-only check has no relationships/views/scope.
- **`validate` on the full workspace (with views)** → fails, but only because of a parser bug (below), not the files.

## Caveats — MCP server limitations, not file issues

1. **Filesystem disabled** — `!include`/`!docs` are standard Structurizr DSL and work with the full tooling; this MCP server just can't resolve them from disk, so I inlined for the check.
2. **Cross-reference bug** — the parser cannot resolve *any* name-based reference: views fail with `The software system "X" does not exist`, and relationships fail with `The source element "X" does not exist` (I tested every form — by name, by ID, model-level, in-block, all element types). So views/relationships can't be verified through this server, though the files use standard DSL.
3. **Syntax** — I wrote descriptions after the name and nested containers inside the `softwareSystem` block (both valid standard DSL) because this parser rejects in-block descriptions and the `within` keyword.

The convention itself (separate files + `!include` + `!docs`) is set up correctly, and the model validates cleanly. If you want, I can also export the views to Mermaid/PlantUML — though that will hit the same cross-reference limitation on this server.
